title: Live-streaming of court proceedings - the pros and cons for litigants
p1: What if anyone could watch your court hearing from anywhere? Courtrooms, once closed spaces, are slowly becoming more accessible through live-streaming. But greater transparency also brings new questions for people fighting cases.
p2: Many assume live-streaming only benefits the public. The reality is more complex. It can help litigants see that proceedings are fair and reduce concerns about what happens inside a courtroom. But it may also expose sensitive arguments, personal details, or emotional moments to a much wider audience.
p3: The surprising part? A hearing is not just about legal arguments; it is also about people, reputations, and privacy. For litigants, live-streaming can create trust in the justice system while requiring careful safeguards to protect confidential information. The real challenge is finding the balance between transparency and dignity.
conclusion: Should court proceedings be live-streamed by default, or should litigants have a say before their hearings are broadcast?
